findings.situation: A filer with an overpayment of $500 on line 34 can enter $800 for the refund, or enter a refund when line 33 does not exceed line 24 and there is no overpayment, and the answer is still accepted.
findings.source_text: f1040 (2025) p.2, line 35a: "Amount of line 34 you want refunded to you"; line 34: "If line 33 is more than line 24, subtract line 24 from line 33. This is the amount you overpaid"; line 36: "Amount of line 34 you want applied to your 2026 estimated tax"
findings.why: Line 35a is a portion of line 34, so it cannot exceed line 34. Together with line 36 it cannot exceed line 34, and it must be zero when there is no overpayment. The accepted answer NonNegDollars sets no upper bound.
findings.bound: 0 <= line35a <= line34 - line36 (and line35a = 0 when line 33 <= line 24)

findings.situation: A filer whose line 34 overpayment is $300, or who has no overpayment, could still enter $1,000, because the accepted answer has no upper limit.
findings.source_text: f1040 (2025) p.2: "34 If line 33 is more than line 24, subtract line 24 from line 33. This is the amount you overpaid"; "36 Amount of line 34 you want applied to your 2026 estimated tax"
findings.why: Line 36 can only be a part of the line 34 overpayment, so its value is capped by line 34. NonNegDollars accepts any non-negative amount, so it allows entries above the overpayment.
findings.bound: 0 to line 34 (and 0 when line 33 does not exceed line 24)

findings.situation: A parent elects on Form 8814 to report a child's dividends, and the child's qualified dividends must be included in the line 3a total, but the question points the filer only to their own Form 1099-DIV box 1b and the line 3a exceptions.
findings.source_text: i1040gi p. 25, Line 3a: "If you are including your child's qualified dividends in the total on line 3a, check box 1 on line 3c. For more information, see the Instructions for Form 8814."
findings.why: The wording does not mention the child's qualified dividends included through Form 8814. A filer answering truthfully from their own 1099-DIV box 1b would leave them out. The line 3a total that feeds the QDCGT worksheet, Schedule D line 22 and the line 16 tax would then be understated.

findings.situation: A filer whose 1099-DIV box 1b includes dividends on stock held less than 61 days, or dividends received as a nominee, cannot tell whether to remove them.
findings.source_text: Question: "after the line 3a exceptions. Supplied as a subtotal; qualification checks are outside this stage." i1040gi p. 26: "Some dividends may be reported as qualified dividends in box 1b of Form 1099-DIV but aren't qualified dividends."
findings.why: "After the line 3a exceptions" tells the filer to remove the excepted dividends, but "qualification checks are outside this stage" can be read as "enter box 1b unchecked." Nothing downstream applies the exceptions, so the second reading overstates line 3a.

findings.situation: A filer married at the end of 2025 to a spouse who was a nonresident alien at some time in 2025 (no election to treat the spouse as a resident), living with that spouse and paying over half the cost of a home for a child or dependent relative, is told by the help to take the first true line and so answers `mfs`, although the text lets them file as head of household.
findings.source_text: i1040gi p. 14, Head of Household: "You are considered unmarried for this purpose if any of the following applies. ... You are married and your spouse was a nonresident alien at any time during the year and the election to treat the alien spouse as a resident alien is not made."
findings.why: The help's only exception to 'take the first line that is true' is living apart for the last six months with a child, so it omits the nonresident alien spouse route to head of household. Such a filer is steered to `mfs`, which changes the tax rates and shuts off the deductions and credits the lines deny to married filing separately.
